steps.title: Start with one named source surface
steps.explanation: Select the right humerus before assigning any material property. Its 2,233 vertices and 3,784 triangles identify the selected source representation, not a stiffness, cartilage field or joint axis. The display rotates the atlas frame only.
steps.observe: Only the humerus is visible. Its name, original OBJ hash and topology counts remain available beside the scene.

steps.title: Separate a muscle surface from its architecture
steps.explanation: Now isolate the short head of biceps brachii. The 1,739 source vertices bound an atlas surface; they do not reveal fascicle direction, tendon slack length or maximum force. Those would require separate measurements or declared model assumptions.
steps.observe: The selected surface and provenance change to the short biceps head: 1,739 vertices and 1,856 triangles. No fibre or force field appears.

steps.title: Assemble evidence without inventing a subject
steps.explanation: Restore the three bones and seven muscle surfaces in their shared atlas coordinates. This is a constructed reference atlas, independent of the recorded OpenArm participant and the Arm26 actuator model. Coincident display is not registration.
steps.observe: The ten surfaces retain 13,852 vertices and 20,218 triangles. Subject registration and clinical validation both read false.

audit.finding: Numeric part IDs and a generic atlas label obscured the difference between named surface identity, muscle architecture and subject matching.
audit.change: Named controls and a bone → muscle → assembly sequence expose original counts, hashes, units and evidence limits.
audit.remaining: No measured fibre map, tendon material field, functional joint axis, subject registration or clinical validation is added.
